q: Why are we losing money in September when every order has a positive margin?
answer:
You aren’t wrong about per-order margins — the books show every order with positive contribution — but overall P&L in September was still a loss because total ad spend and other P&L lines outweighed that contribution. Net profit (order-date) for 1–30 Sep 2026 was a loss of ₹2,86,296 (previous 30-day window 2–31 Aug: loss of ₹7,73,786), so the business remained unprofitable on the month level even though orders were individually profitable.

What’s behind it
- Big driver: ad spend overwhelmed contribution. Ad spend (P&L basis) fell from ₹22,03,894 → ₹11,93,322, while contribution fell from ₹14,30,108 → ₹9,07,026; the move in ad spend and contribution together explain the swing to the smaller loss in September.  
- Revenue fell: P&L gross/net sales fell (gross sales and net sales dropped ~44.5%), shrinking the contribution pool available to cover fixed and ad costs.  
- Platform mix mattered: Meta and Google together account for most of the movement (Meta and Google ad/platform splits account for the majority of the change in net profit). The period-level decomposition in the data reconciles exactly to the net-profit change (the change is an accounting identity, not a speculation).

Worth checking:
- Which campaigns or product groups bought the most attributed contribution vs spend (break down by ad platform → campaign → product). That will show whether spend is buying low-margin sales or simply there’s not enough sales volume to cover fixed costs.

Period: 2026-09-01..2026-09-30 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-29
